subject: Meteorology
title: Wind Shear on Approach
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Wind Shear on Approach.

hook.text: Wind shear on final approach is a sudden change in wind speed or direction—causing dangerous airspeed fluctuations.

buildup.text: A decreasing headwind or sudden tailwind robs airspeed—the aircraft sinks below the glidepath with little warning.

discovery.text: Low-Level Wind Shear Alert Systems (LLWAS) at airports detect dangerous shear and warn controllers and pilots.

twist.text: Some wind shear is too localized for LLWAS—pilots must recognize the signs and execute an immediate go-around.

climax.text: Modern aircraft have predictive wind shear systems—alerting pilots seconds before encountering the shear.

punchline.text: A gust of wind at the wrong moment—catch it or go around.

quiz.question: What should a pilot do when encountering wind shear on approach?
